Determine the exact value of $\sin\alpha$ using the fundamental trigonometric identity with $\cos\alpha = \frac{8}{17}$:
$$\sin\alpha = \sqrt{1 - \cos^2\alpha} = \sqrt{1 - \left(\frac{8}{17}\right)^2} = \sqrt{\frac{289 - 64}{289}} = \sqrt{\frac{225}{289}} = \frac{15}{17}$$

Substitute the exact values into the reciprocal expression:
$$\frac{1}{\sin\alpha} + \frac{1}{\tan\alpha} = \frac{1}{\frac{15}{17}} + \frac{1}{\frac{15}{8}} = \frac{17}{15} + \frac{8}{15}$$

Add the fractions with common denominator:
$$= \frac{17 + 8}{15} = \frac{25}{15} = \frac{5}{3}$$
